works.title: Get Up (I Feel Like Being a) Sex Machine

position_in_era.primary_genre_lineage: funk / soul — rhythmic deconstruction of R&B
position_in_era.geographic_locus: King Studios, Cincinnati, Ohio / Apollo Theater, Harlem
position_in_era.historical_role: James Brown invented the rhythmic grammar of funk with "Cold Sweat" (1967) — stripping harmony to a minimum and centering the groove entirely on the drum/bass interlock — establishing the percussive vocabulary that would flow through disco, hip-hop, and every downstream genre including Miss You.

narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Drummer Clyde Stubblefield joined Brown in 1965 and became the engine of the funk era; Questlove later called him "the one who defined funk music." Saxophonist-arranger Alfred "Pee Wee" Ellis co-wrote "Cold Sweat" and shaped the horn-driven architecture of the JBs sound. Maceo Parker's saxophone became the signature voice of Brown's live band.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: The Apollo Theater in Harlem was Brown's cathedral — his 1962 live album there documented the raw funk aesthetic before it had a name. King Studios in Cincinnati was where the foundational recordings happened under direct Brown control as producer.
narrative_slots.production_facts: Brown produced all sessions himself at King Studios, enforcing his famous fining system for musicians who missed a note or left the groove. "Cold Sweat" was recorded in May 1967 and reached #1 R&B, #7 Hot 100. "Funky Drummer" was recorded November 20, 1969 in Cincinnati; its 20-second drum break by Stubblefield has been sampled on over 1,300 songs.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: The Funky Drummer break was improvised by Clyde Stubblefield — an unrepeated live improv that became the single most-sampled drum performance in music history, appearing on records by Public Enemy, Beastie Boys, N.W.A, George Michael, and hundreds more.
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: "Cold Sweat" was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame in 2016. The funk vocabulary Brown established in 1967-1970 is the shared ancestor of both the disco movement and the hip-hop sampling tradition.
